solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Clean windows in parsonage energetically at first

indicators.note: 'at first' asks for the opening letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Someone cleans the vicarage windows with vigour before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe something is to rub it clean with a cloth, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Know-it-alls rejecting outsiders twist new ropes

indicators.note: rejecting outsiders means throwing out the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: taken as written, then stripped of its outer letters
the same rejection of outsiders applies to new, leaving only its middle letter
guys are guy ropes, the ropes that hold a tent steady

explanation.surface: Smart alecks, refusing help from outside, show newcomers a novel way to twist ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejecting outsiders' acts on both of the next two words, so new keeps only its middle letter too; 'ropes' is not the anagram it might suggest but tent guys.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiseguys are people who act as though they know everything: smart alecks who think they are clever.

clue.text: Cut a serrated edge in flower

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cut a zigzag edge in cloth
second meaning: a garden plant of the carnation family

explanation.surface: A gardener or florist trims a flower with a zigzag cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinking shears give fabric a zigzag edge, and pinks are scented garden plants related to carnations.

clue.text: Tip Rose extravagantly for clever remark

indicators.note: doing something extravagantly suggests wild excess, so the letters are flung into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rose the waitress earns a lavish tip for her witty comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp reply, borrowed from the fencer's counter-thrust.

clue.text: Withdraw from suspect decree

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious and not in proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone backs away from an official order of doubtful legitimacy.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to move back or pull away, a synonym of withdrawing.

clue.text: Drinking establishments in dodgy US police hubs

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are bent out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bars turn up inside corrupt American police stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Public house is the full British name for a pub, a place licensed to sell alcohol.

clue.text: Frank starts to empty drawers everywhere in rush

parts.note: to frank a letter is to stamp it

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters

parts.note: the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: Frank empties every drawer in a mad hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank reads as a man's name but is the verb for marking a letter with postage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden mass rush, as of panicked cattle or a crowd.

clue.text: Current running backwards in section of damaged dynamo

indicators.note: a section of the words is a run of letters sitting inside them

parts.note: found across the junction of the two words

explanation.surface: An electric current is flowing the wrong way in a broken generator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running backwards' looks like a reversal signal, but it belongs to the definition; the letters read forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirl of water or air moving against the main flow.

clue.text: Score twice showing good vision

parts.note: a score is twenty
the same number again

explanation.surface: Someone who hits the target twice demonstrates a sharp eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal sharpness of eyesight is called twenty-twenty after the standard eye-chart measure.

clue.text: Something used in advertising snack food by executives

parts.note: a light meal between slices of bread
the board of directors runs a company

explanation.surface: Company bosses promote a snack product in an ad campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandwich board is a pair of hinged placards worn front and back by someone advertising in the street.

clue.text: Professor returned to signal agreement

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: An academic came back to give the go-ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipping the head is a gesture of assent, so to nod is to show agreement.

clue.text: Worry leading group

parts.note: a team that is ahead is said to be up
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about the band at the top of the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to trouble or distress them, a synonym of worry as a verb.

clue.text: Newspaper and packs of cards in relaxation areas

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a deck is a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers lounge with papers and card games.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundecks are open decks or terraces where people lie in the sun and unwind.

clue.text: Outdoes former top players, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the sound of the phrase matters rather than its spelling

parts.note: ex means former, and seeds are the top-ranked players in a tournament

explanation.surface: Someone surpasses tennis players who used to be ranked highly.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed is to go beyond, so a thing that exceeds another surpasses it.

clue.text: Guide woman parking her Ford at the back

parts.note: the female pronoun
P is the road-sign symbol for parking
taken as written

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A woman directs someone to park her Ford car round the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To shepherd people is to lead or herd them along, as a shepherd moves a flock.

clue.text: Politician chosen — a Tory to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only part of the letters is taken

parts.note: runs from the end of the first word through to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A selected politician is partly a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected legislator.

clue.text: Manipulated price over European formula

indicators.note: manipulated figures have been worked over and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A rigged price is placed above a European pricing formula.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' would usually place one part on top of another; here the order happens to match plain sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of instructions for a result, figuratively a formula for success.

clue.text: Abnormally large gong regularly askew

parts.note: a gong is slang for a medal or honour, such as the OBE (Order of the British Empire)

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A huge gong hangs crooked again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means extremely overweight, a medical term for unusual bodily size.

clue.text: Bird hiding in chrysanthemums

indicators.note: something hiding in a word is tucked inside it, concealed among its letters

parts.note: sits near the end of the word

explanation.surface: A bird is lurking in the flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird, an example of the category.

clue.text: Established company

definitions.meaning: first meaning: solidly fixed and settled

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of a long-standing business; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as an adjective for something securely fixed and as a noun for a commercial business.

clue.text: Book everyone for dance party

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone reserves tickets for the whole group to go dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a formal social gathering held for dancing.

clue.text: Lacking in care, I decorate inns badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters end up jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A careless decorator confesses to doing a poor job on some pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inconsiderate gives no thought to other people's feelings, so lacks care for them.

clue.text: Accidentally enter foggy outskirts of Penzance

parts.note: a synonym

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so the first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles into the fog-bound edge of a Cornish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is a seaside town in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistype is to key in text wrongly by accident.

clue.text: Good boy is happy

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A well-behaved child is cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad is a synonym of pleased or cheerful.
